title: Factored Cognition Monitoring at Different Decomposition Granularities

original_idea.body:
# Factored Cognition Monitoring at Different Decomposition Granularities

**Problem:** Factor(T,U) shows decomposing a task into isolated child-tasks boosts trusted-monitoring safety from 41% to 63%. But the safety gain presumably depends on how finely the task is decomposed, and finer decomposition costs usefulness — this trade-off is unmapped.

**Direction:** Implement a minimal Factor(T,U) on APPS coding tasks with an open trusted decomposer and untrusted solver. Vary decomposition granularity (whole task, 2 subtasks, fine-grained subtasks) and measure attack success rate and usefulness at each granularity. Find the knee of the safety-usefulness curve.

**Why it matters:** Gives a concrete recommendation for how aggressively to factor tasks under monitoring — actionable for anyone deploying agentic coding assistants. Reuses APPS; inference-only; extends a 2025/26 protocol along an unexplored axis.

**Relevant context:** Factor(T,U): Factored Cognition Strengthens Monitoring of Untrusted AI (arXiv 2512.02157): trusted model decomposes, untrusted solves isolated child-tasks; safety 41%->63%. Uses APPS-style backdoor evaluation.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: granularity safety/usefulness knee gives actionable factoring recommendation.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Implementing Factor(T,U) decomposer/solver pipeline needs solid ML and guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused granularity sweep but requires building the factored pipeline.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Extends a protocol along an unexplored axis, public APPS.

novelty.reasoning: Factor(T,U) published; granularity-tradeoff axis may be open.
